newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-BICHEL SHINES AS QUEENSLAND TAKE CONTROL.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-BICHEL SHINES AS QUEENSLAND TAKE CONTROL.

text.p: Pace bowler Andrew Bichel continued to press his claims for a place in the international squad as he led Queensland into a dominant position in their Sheffield Shield match against Victoria on Sunday.
Bichel, who took five for 46 in Victoria's first innings of 162, added another four as Victoria struggled to 268 for nine at the end of the third day of their four-day match.
Victoria resumed on 54 for no wicket in response to Queensland's first innings 305. Opener Warren Ayres top-scored with 56 before falling to Bichel, who finished with four for 64 from 33 overs.
Bichel later told reporters his goal was to force his way into the Australia squad for next year's Ashes tour of England.
"I made that goal a long time ago, it is the ultimate," he said.
Former Australia batsman Dean Jones again failed, adding three to his first innings duck before falling to Bichel for the second time in the match.

In Adelaide, James Brayshaw and Geoff Parker led a South Australia fightback in the match against Western Australia. South Australia were 325 for nine at stumps and held a lead of 284 going into the final day.
Brayshaw just missed scoring his 11th first-class century and was dismissed for 96 as he attempted to pull a delivery from spin bowler Brad Hogg. Parker was 80 not out at the close.
In Hobart, New South Wales lost two early second innings wickets but were still in a strong position against Tasmania, ending the day on 70 for two for an overall lead of 146.
Tasmania captain David Boon had earlier declared his side's first innings closed at 327 for nine in the hope of forcing a result in the rain-affected match.
Shaun Young top-scored for Tasmania with 108 not out.
